neighbours.label: alternative paths and player choice in games and interactive stories (branching, routes, optional areas, multiple endings)
fire: In this adventure game, every conversation splits into branching paths that change the ending.
The visual novel offers a separate route for each of the four main characters.
Players can pick between two alternate paths through the swamp level.
This puzzle book lets readers decide which chapter to read next, leading to eleven possible endings.
Hidden behind the waterfall is an optional area with extra treasure.
Your decisions in the first act determine which faction trusts you later.
The quest tree branches three times, so a single playthrough sees only part of the story.
At the crossroads the player may choose the mountain trail or the river road.
quiet: In this adventure game, every conversation moves the plot steadily toward the same ending.
The visual novel tells one fixed story about the four main characters.
Players walk through the swamp level from the entrance to the exit.
This puzzle book is read from the first chapter to the last in order.
Behind the waterfall the hero finds the key needed to open the gate.
The first act introduces the factions and their long history of war.
The quest is short, and a single playthrough takes about two hours.
At the crossroads the hero meets an old merchant selling maps.

notes: Card: branching dialogue, a character's route, paths followed by the application, optional area, as long as you wish. Probe: 'no choices' and 'as you wish' also fire, so the concept of choosing between alternatives, not one word. Near misses describe linear games without choice vocabulary.
